page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration includes 16 physical CPU cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading, paired with 128 GB of RAM to yield 4 GB of memory per core. Hardware features include AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI vector extensions alongside AES encryption support. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and operates without attached GPU acceleration, relying on network bandwidth rated at a baseline of 10 Gbps.

Performance testing reflects average overall multi-core compute and memory capabilities. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 28006.29 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10179.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 108.04 GB/sec for large uncached read blocks and 47.67 GB/sec for large write blocks. PassMark metrics scored 27100.23 for CPU and 2522.22 for memory operations. Single-threaded performance exhibits a bottleneck, with single-core stress-ng tests and gzip compression registering in the lower quartile of baseline performance.

The ecs.g6.8xlarge instance offers resource density suitable for balanced workloads requiring predictable compute and RAM ratios. Because local storage is absent, external block storage must be utilized, impacting overall infrastructure architecture. The system demonstrates solid throughput in application-level benchmarks, such as 26.79 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.21 GB/sec in static web serving. Workload fit includes web application hosting, middle-tier enterprise services, memory-cached database layers, software compilation, and general-purpose microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge is a general-purpose x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading, it offers 128 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per thread. The server incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, though it lacks dedicated GPU hardware and local storage capabilities. Networking performance is established at a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmarks highlight solid, average multi-core CPU capacity and memory bandwidth, alongside high execution throughput in Redis operations and software compilation. However, single-core CPU throughput remains relatively weak. Designed without ephemeral local disk drives, it relies entirely on remote block storage. Overall, this server configuration provides dependable resource density tailored for general-purpose enterprise applications, web serving, microservices, and database workloads.
